lesson_title: Measurement, Maps, Data and Probability Essentials: Buy Enough, Not Too Much
hook_text: The maths says 11,7 boxes of tiles. Buy 11 and you FAIL the floor. Here's the rounding rule shops never teach.
clip_script: The main room's floor: 5,2 by 3,6 — 18,72 square metres of tiling to do. Boxes cover 1,6 square metres each, so the job needs 11,7 boxes. And here is the whole topic in one decision: you cannot buy 0,7 of a box, and 11 boxes leaves bare screed in front of the window. Twelve boxes. Always UP, never nearest — the shop rounds your change in its favour; you round the boxes up in the floor's favour. Twelve at R210: R2 520 on the list. Paint plays the same game with a twist: 13,5 square metres of wall, but TWO coats means the roller travels 27 — the quiet detail buried mid-sentence that doubles the answer. Measure, match units, round up to what the shop actually sells, price it.
visual_style: Tiles snapping onto a floor grid that stops one patch short at 11 boxes, the bare patch flashing red by the window, then a twelfth box sliding in to complete it as the total price stamps down.
pacing: Quick area build, tense freeze on the bare patch, clean resolve with the round-up rule and price stamp.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson to cost, map, summarise and judge with numbers on your side.
